segments: 356. Chronography of Barhebraeus.
al-Malik as-Salih sent to him and sought peace,
on the condition that he, Saladin, should rule over Damascus, Hama, and Homs,
and the rest of Syria, that is to say the outer part, he should leave to as-Salih.
And when Saladin would not agree,
he added to his share also Ma'arra and Kafr Tab.
And he consented, and swore
that in all the lands under his control the proclamation (khutbah) of Sultan al-Malik as-Salih should be celebrated,
and whenever occasion required, he would come to his aid.
And when the Caliph heard of Saladin's victory,
he sent him royal vestments, a sword, banners, and a diploma of sultanate.
And at that time, Qutb al-Din Qaymaz, one of the emirs of Baghdad, rebelled against the Caliph al-Mustadi;
and he gathered his men and launched an attack against the palace of the Caliph.
Then the Caliph, being terrified,
went up to the roof,
and commanded a herald,
and he proclaimed with a loud voice:
"O sons of Baghdad,
behold, the time has come for you to aid your lord and the head of your faith,
and to show your zeal on behalf of your faith!"
And the cry went forth throughout the city,
and they all assembled with swords, staves, bricks, and slings,
and put Qaymaz and those with him to flight.
And when they fled into the wilderness, they became thirsty,
and they found water in a certain cistern wherein serpents had drowned.
And when they drank from it,
they all fell ill, along with their horses.
And they set their faces toward Mosul,
and many of them perished on the road,
and even those who reached Mosul did not survive.
And in the same year, which was 1486,
1486 of the Greeks [1174/1175 AD],
the Armenian grandees of Cilicia revolted against Mleh, ruler of Cilicia,
and sought to kill him.
And when he became aware of this,
he fled to one of the fortresses.
However, the guards of the fortress, knowing what evils the Christians had suffered and were suffering from him,
seized him and dismembered him,
and cast him to the dogs.
Then the grandees brought his brother's son, Roupen (or Roubel?) son of Stephen, from Tarsus,
and made him king over them.
Then he killed the murderers of his uncle Mleh,
saying, "Because they threw him to the dogs,
and did not bury him when they killed him."
